content.title: About
content.content: Dirty rice is a classic Creole dish from Louisiana, consisting of rice sautéed with ground meat (often turkey, beef or pork), browned offal, green onions, and a blend of spices. The name comes from the dark color the dish acquires from the blood and browned organ meats, giving it a rich, savory flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in the 19th‑century African‑American communities of Louisiana, using inexpensive organ meats.
The word “dirty” refers to the color, not to the quality of the food.
Many variations exist: turkey, chicken, shrimp, or even a vegetarian version with mushrooms.
Dirty rice is commonly served as a side to fried meats, seafood, or Creole soups.
Traditional recipes often included blood sausage, intensifying the “dirty” hue.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The meat and offal provide a substantial amount of complete protein, essential for tissue repair and growth.

items.title: Rich source of iron
items.content: Blood‑rich organ meats contain heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and whole‑grain rice supply B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber from rice
items.content: Rice, especially when whole‑grain, adds fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: The dish contains no added sugars, making it suitable for moderate‑carb diets.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Traditional recipes often use soy sauce or generous salt, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Cholesterol levels
items.content: Offal and fatty meats can raise cholesterol if consumed frequently.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Shrimp or crab versions may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improperly cooked organ meats may harbor pathogens; thorough cooking is essential.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve dirty rice hot as a main dish or as a side to fried meats, fish, or Creole soups. Garnish with fresh parsley or green onions and add a dash of hot sauce if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, portion into containers and freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before serving.
